topics.name: Inversion after never, seldom, hardly, not only
Degrees of comparison and 'the more ... the more'
Word forms: adjective, adverb and noun

options: I wish I can fly like an eagle.
I wish I could flew like an eagle.
I wish I could fly like an eagle.
questions.rule: A wish about something impossible now takes could + base verb: I wish I could fly.

options: Animals does not complain about their condition.
Animals do not complains about their condition.
Animals do not complain about their condition.
questions.rule: Plural subject takes do not, and after do not the verb stays in the base form: complain.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After does not, use the base form of the verb: does not sleep.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Comparing one with all others in a group (in the world) needs the superlative: the biggest.

questions.after: a bird for just one day.
questions.rule: For an unreal wish about the present, use were: I wish I were a bird.
To describe how someone walked, we need an adverb: slowly.
Never goes before the main verb: Animals never complain.

chat: Do you ever wish you were a bird?
options: Yes, I wish I could fly over the hills.
Yes, I wish I can flying over the hills.
Yes, I wishing I could fly over the hills.
questions.rule: Use I wish I could + base verb for something you cannot do now.

questions.prompt: Change into a negative sentence without changing the meaning.
questions.source: Animals are content with what they have.
options: Animals are not content with what they have.
Animals are not discontented with what they have.
Animals is not discontented with what they have.
questions.rule: Add not and use the opposite word (content to discontented) so the meaning stays the same.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this paragraph.
questions.rule: One dog (Bruno, he) takes singular forms: does not lie and sleeps.

options: Seldom our cat leaves the garden.
Seldom does our cat leaves the garden.
Seldom does our cat leave the garden.
questions.rule: After Seldom at the start, use question order: does + subject + base verb.

options: The more you feed the cat, the lazier it gets.
The more you feed the cat, the lazy it gets.
More you feed the cat, the lazier it gets.
questions.rule: The pattern is the + comparative ..., the + comparative: the more ..., the lazier.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: To say how she watched, use an adverb: very carefully.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: A wish about the past takes the past perfect: wishes she had seen.

questions.after: the dog guard the house, but it also plays with the children.
questions.rule: After Not only at the start, use question order; the dog is singular, so does.
wishes + he could + base verb expresses a wish about the present.

chat: Which is faster, the cheetah or the horse?
options: The cheetah is more faster than the horse.
The cheetah is fastest than the horse.
The cheetah is faster than the horse.
questions.rule: Comparing two things: faster than. Never use more with -er.

chat: Do cats complain about their food?
options: No, they doesn't complain about it.
No, they don't complain about it.
No, they don't complains about it.
questions.rule: They takes don't, and after don't use the base verb: don't complain.

questions.source: The cheetah is the fastest land animal.
options: The cheetah is faster than any land animal.
The cheetah is fast than any other land animal.
The cheetah is faster than any other land animal.
questions.rule: Superlative to comparative: faster than any other. 'Other' is needed because the cheetah is itself a land animal.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this paragraph.
questions.rule: Not one of them is singular: is. They takes the plain verb: never whine.

options: Their simple is a lesson for all of us.
Their simplicity is a lesson for all of us.
Their simply is a lesson for all of us.
questions.rule: After their, as the subject, we need a noun: simplicity.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After Seldom, use question order. A cat is singular, so: Seldom does a cat sleep.
Both halves need a comparative: the more ..., the more.
If only works like wish: for an unreal present, use were.

questions.prompt: Make a sentence that begins with 'Not once'.
questions.rule: After Not once, use question order: did + subject + base verb.

chat: Have you ever seen a white tiger?
options: No, never I have seen one.
No, never have I saw one.
No, never have I seen one.
questions.rule: With never first, the helper comes before the subject: never have I seen.

chat: How did the puppy behave at the vet's?
questions.rule: Behaved is an action verb, so describe it with an adverb: calmly.

questions.prompt: Change into an affirmative sentence without changing the meaning.
questions.rule: Not one ... dissatisfied = Every ... satisfied. Every takes a singular noun and verb.

questions.source: I have never seen such a peaceful horse.
options: Never I have seen such a peaceful horse.
Never had I seen such a peaceful horse.
Never have I seen such a peaceful horse.
questions.rule: Move never to the front and invert: Never have I seen. Keep the tense (have, not had).

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this paragraph.
questions.rule: Past wish: had visited. The cows (plural): complain. Not one of them (singular): lies.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct question tag.
options: Animals do not lie awake at night, don't they?
Animals do not lie awake at night, do they?
Animals do not lie awake at night, does they?
questions.rule: A negative sentence takes a positive tag. Animals = they, so: do they?

options: No other animal is loved as more as the dog.
No other animal is loved as much as the dog.
No other animal are loved as much as the dog.
questions.rule: Positive degree: as much as. No other animal is singular, so is loved.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Hardly had ... when is followed by the simple past: when it jumped.
The passive verb are looked after is described by an adverb: are carefully looked after.

questions.after: kept a dog when he was young.
questions.rule: A wish about the past (when he was young) uses the past perfect: had kept.

questions.prompt: Make a sentence with a question tag.
questions.rule: Negative statement + positive tag: doesn't like ..., does it?

chat: Is a tortoise as fast as a rabbit?
options: No, a tortoise is not as fast as a rabbit.
No, a tortoise is not as faster as a rabbit.
No, a tortoise is not so fast than a rabbit.
questions.rule: Positive degree uses the plain adjective: not as fast as. Never as ... than.

questions.source: The elephant is stronger than the horse.
options: The horse is not as strong as the elephant.
The horse is not as stronger as the elephant.
The elephant is not as strong as the horse.
questions.rule: Start with the weaker one: The horse is not as strong as the elephant. The meaning stays the same.

questions.source: Our dog does not bite strangers.
options: Strangers are not bit by our dog.
Strangers are not bitten by our dog.
Strangers is not bitten by our dog.
questions.rule: Simple present passive: are not + past participle (bitten). Strangers is plural: are.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this paragraph.
questions.rule: The more ..., the more. After could, base verb: keep. Not one of her rabbits is singular: has.

options: Not only the dog guards the house, but it also brings in the newspaper.
Not only does the dog guards the house, but it also brings in the newspaper.
Not only does the dog guard the house, but it also brings in the newspaper.
questions.rule: Not only at the start needs inversion: does the dog guard (base verb after does).

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: and joins two nouns of the same kind: patience and gentleness.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: One of the most ... is always followed by a plural noun: dogs.

questions.before: No sooner had the cat seen the dog
questions.rule: No sooner is always paired with than (hardly goes with when).

questions.prompt: Make a sentence that begins with 'Seldom'.
questions.rule: After Seldom, invert: have I met. A more + adjective comes before the noun.

chat: Would you rather be a bird or a fish?
options: I would rather to be a bird than a fish.
I would rather being a bird than a fish.
I would rather be a bird than a fish.
questions.rule: Would rather is followed by the base verb without to: would rather be.

chat: Didn't the dog bark at the postman today?
options: No, it didn't barked at him at all.
No, it doesn't barked at him at all.
No, it didn't bark at him at all.
questions.rule: Past negative: didn't + base verb (bark), never didn't barked.

questions.source: Only a patient person can tame a horse.
options: None but a patient person cannot tame a horse.
None but a patient person can tame a horse.
None but a patient person can tames a horse.
questions.rule: Only becomes None but; the verb stays positive: can tame.

questions.source: Very few animals are as loyal as the dog.
options: The dog is the most loyal animal.
The dog is one of the most loyal animals.
The dog is one of the most loyal animal.
questions.rule: Very few ... as ... as becomes one of the most ... + plural noun, not simply the most.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this paragraph.
questions.rule: Animals is plural: Not only do animals. They complain. The longer ..., the more peaceful.
